title: Those vows still terminate on Saints too—like alms to Christ in the poor; same promise, different end (latria vs dulia)
source_text: XXXI. Nihilominus pertendit vota illa quae fiunt Deo in Sanctis non terminari ad solum Deum, sed etiam ad ipsos Sanctos, quemadmodum eleemosyna quae datur Christo in paupere, vere datur ipsi pauperi. Ac ut ostendat in eo nullam esse Idololatriam, dicit non eadem ratione votum fieri Sanctis, & Deo. Nam Sanctis quidem aliquid vere & proprie promitti, quemadmodum proprie & vere Deo promittitur: Verum non eodem fine, neque eadem mente aliquid Deo & Sanctis promitti. Nempe quia, quum aliquis Deo quippiam vovet & promittit, id facit in signum gratitudinis erga primum principium omnium bonorum, & in recognitionem beneficii ab ipso, tanquam a primo authore accepti, & proinde illa promissio est cultus Latriae; at Sanctis promittitur aliquid in signum gratitudinis solum erga mediatores, & intercessores, per quos a Deo beneficia accepimus; & proinde illa promissio non est cultus Latriae sed Duliae.
pass_a_gloss: Nevertheless he contends that those vows which are made to God in the Saints do not terminate on God alone, but also on the Saints themselves, just as the alms which is given to Christ in the poor is truly given to the poor man himself. And that he may show there is no Idolatry in that, he says a vow is not made to the Saints and to God by the same reason. For indeed something is truly and properly promised to the Saints, just as it is properly and truly promised to God: But something is not promised to God and to the Saints by the same end, nor with the same mind. Namely because, when someone vows and promises anything to God, he does it in sign of gratitude toward the first principle of all goods, and in recognition of a benefit received from Him as from the first author, and therefore that promise is the cult of Latria; but to the Saints something is promised in sign of gratitude only toward mediators and intercessors through whom we have received benefits from God; and therefore that promise is not the cult of Latria but of Dulia.
pass_b_english: Even ‘God-in-the-Saints’ vows still land on the Saints—as alms to Christ in the poor land on the poor.
Same true promise, different end: God as first author (latria) vs Saints as mediators (dulia).

lemmas.latin: eleemosyna quae datur Christo in paupere
lemmas.gloss: alms which is given to Christ in the poor

choices.why: Blocks idolatry charge while keeping dual termination.
